info.name: Postman Collection for Sophos Firewall
info.description:
# Postman collection for Sophos Firewall APIs

This Postman collection helps you interact with Sophos Firewall APIs. Sophos Firewall API allows developers to use programs to do GET, ADD, UPDATE, and DELETE operations in the firewall. The API uses XML (eXtensible Markup Language) to exchange data between the firewall and the program.

⚠️The Postman API collection is a subset of the API requests that the firewall supports. For the complete set of APIs, see [Sophos Firewall API help](https://docs.sophos.com/nsg/sophos-firewall/19.5/API/index.html).

## Getting started

1. Create an API administrator with read-write permissions for the modules you want.
2. To accept the administrator's API calls, allow their IP address in the firewall.

See [How to use API](https://docs.sophos.com/nsg/sophos-firewall/Latest/Help/en-us/webhelp/onlinehelp/index.html?contextId=API-how-to-use)

## Install Postman

Install the latest stable version of Postman.

## Import the collection

Click `Import` and paste the following URL: `https://doc.sophos.com/nsg/sophos-firewall/api-collections/sophosfirewall.postman_collection.json`

Postman imports the collection.

Alternatively, go to the URL, right-click the file content, click `Save as` to save the file in a text editor, and import the file to Postman.

## Set up your Postman environment

In the collection's main menu, click **Variables**, and change the following initial or current values based on your requirement, then click **Save**:

1. username
2. password
3. firewall's ip address: It's the IP address or hostname of your web admin console.
4. firewall's port

## Make an API authentication request

You're now ready to make your first API call. We recommend that you first verify that the port, IP address, and credentials work.

1. Go to **Collection** > **Authentication** > **Sign in**.
2. In the main body, click **Send**.

You'll get a successful authentication response.

The firewall authenticates your API requests based on the credentials you've updated when setting up the environment. To ensure security, the API client sends your credentials over HTTPS to the firewall. HTTPS provides a secure channel between the client and server, encrypting the data in transit and ensuring that unauthorized actors don't intercept or modify the communication.

## Making configuration requests

You can now send configuration requests. These contain example settings. Make sure you customize these to meet your network requirements.

## API payload

The firewall API uses XML payloads to send and receive data. The firewall uses the HTTP POST method for configuration requests rather than the standard GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE methods. It uses custom XML tags within the payload for specific operations.

For example, when you create a new object in the firewall, make sure the request body includes the `<Set>` tag to specify the object's attributes and values. The firewall accepts only these custom tags, which are transmitted using the HTTP POST method.

## Understanding XML tags in Sophos Firewall API

The custom tags are used in combination with other required tags and attributes.

1. `<Request>`: Use this tag to send a request to the API. The API version is optional and requires version-specific syntax.

   **Example:**

   ```
    <Request APIVersion="1800.2">
        <Login>
            <Username>username</Username>
            <Password>password</Password>
        </Login>
    </Request>

   ```

2. `<Login>`: Use this tag to authenticate API requests with the firewall.
3. `<Set operation="add">` or `<Set operation="update">`: Use these tags to add or update the settings. If you don't specify the "operation" value, the firewall considers it a request to add the data. If the object doesn't support the add functionality, the request doesn't succeed.

   **Example:**

   ```
   <Request>
       <Login>
           <Username>username</Username>
           <Password>password</Password>
       </Login>
       <Set operation="add">
           <IPHost>
               <Name>IPaddress</Name>
               <IPFamily>IPv4</IPFamily>
               <HostType>IP</HostType>
               <IPAddress>1.1.1.1</IPAddress>
           </IPHost>
       </Set>
   </Request>

   ```

6. `<Get>`: Use this tag to get data from the firewall.

    **Example:**

    ```
    <Request>
        <Login>
            <Username>username</Username>
            <Password>password</Password>
        </Login>
        <Get>
            <IPHost></IPHost>
        </Get>
    </Request>

    ```

5. `<Remove>`: Use this tag to delete data from the firewall.

    **Example:**

    ```
    <Request>
        <Login>
        <Username>username</Username>
        <Password>password</Password>
        </Login>
        <Remove>
            <IPHost>
                <Name>CustomName</Name>
            </IPHost>
        </Remove>
    </Request>

    ```

6. `<Filter>`: Use this tag to get data from the firewall based on certain criteria, for example, the object name. Specify the criteria using the `<key>` tag and the attribute values for "name" and "criteria". Supported criteria: [`=`,`!=`,`like`]

    **Example:**

    ```
    Request>
        <Login>
            <Username>username</Username>
            <Password>password</Password>
        </Login>
        <Get>
            <IPHost>
                <Filter>
                    <key name="Name" criteria="like">Name of IP Host</key>
                </Filter>
            </IPHost>
        </Get>
    </Request>

    ```

7. `<Response>`: This tag contains the response to your API request.
8. `<Status>`: This tag is part of the `<Response>` tag and shows the status of your API request.
9. `transactionid`: This attribute ensures the integrity of the request and response transaction. It's an optional attribute used in the `<Set>` tag. If you use it, we recommend using an alphanumeric value.

   **Example:**

   ```
   <Request>
       <Login>
           <Username>username</Username>
           <Password>password</Password>
       </Login>
       <Set transactionid="xyz123">
           <IPHost>
               <Name>IPaddress</Name>
               <IPFamily>IPv4</IPFamily>
               <HostType>IP</HostType>
               <IPAddress>1.1.1.1</IPAddress>
           </IPHost>
       </Set>
   </Request>

   ```

## Security

Use extreme caution in handling and storing your credentials. Compromised passwords allow malicious actors to access or delete sensitive data in your firewall. We recommend that you take the following measures:

1. Use a password manager.
2. Don't use your credentials from an untrusted device or network.
3. Don't share your credentials, especially over insecure channels, such as email.
4. Don't add your password to the source code.

## Feedback

Click `Feedback` at the top of the firewall's web admin console and send your feedback.
